subject: SLA amendment request: temporary uptime threshold and credit cap
messages:
From: Timothy Rosen <timothy.rosen@greenline.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term SLA exception + credit approach for Aug migration

Markus —

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing a regional data migration in early August and expect a short period of elevated error rates while we warm caches and rehydrate prefix/KV caches for high-volume inference flows. Our infra team estimates 24–48 hours of elevated failure/retry behavior (mainly 500s and degraded p95 latency) during the cutover window.

Two asks from Greenline:
- Can Redwood provide a formal, time-bounded SLA exception that temporarily lowers the uptime threshold for August only (we're proposing 99.90% for Aug instead of our current 99.95%)?
- If an exception is acceptable, would Redwood agree to a fixed cap on monthly service credits for that month (Greenline requests a max credit of 5% of monthly invoice) rather than the standard sliding credit schedule?

The goal is to avoid a high, unpredictable credit payout for a planned migration while keeping clear remediation economics. If helpful, I can share the migration runbook and target maintenance window (we're looking at Aug 10–12).

Tim
Timothy Rosen
Head of Infrastructure, Greenline Financial
ops@greenline.com

Attachments: migration_runbook_excerpt.txt (referenced)

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Rosen <timothy.rosen@greenline.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term SLA exception + credit approach for Aug migration

Timothy — thanks for the clear ask and for flagging the window. We're open to a time-limited exception but need to align on two things before we sign off: exact credit calculation (fixed cap vs sliding remedy), and what counts as a scheduled maintenance carveout vs unplanned availability impact.

Quick proposal from our side to speed this along:
- Option A (fixed cap): Redwood agrees to a one-month exception lowering baseline to 99.90% for Aug with a hard credit cap of 5% of the monthly invoice. No further credits are available for that month outside the cap.
- Option B (modified sliding): Keep the sliding remedy but apply a higher threshold for slack in Aug (e.g., escalate credits only for drops below 99.80%) and cap total credits at 7.5%.

If either option is acceptable, we'll prepare a short amendment (1 page) capturing dates, carveouts (scheduled migration window + pre/post warm-up buffers), and the credit cap. I'm attaching a draft amendment (SLA amendment v2) and our credit calculator so you can see how numbers map to invoice amounts.

Laura/Ben — looping you for legal/finance review. Can you weigh in on the cap wording and whether we should propose an escrow/recoupment mechanism instead?

Next steps: confirm which option Greenline prefers and the exact maintenance window. Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week.

—Markus
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla_amendment_greenline_v2.pdf (draft), service_credit_calculator.xlsx

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term SLA exception + credit approach for Aug migration

Markus / Ben —

Thanks for the context. High level guidance from legal: we can do a 1-month amendment but need explicit language on the maintenance carveout window, notification obligations, and a firm cap on dollar exposure. Finance prefers a cap expressed as the lesser of X% of monthly invoice OR a dollar amount. Suggested wording: 

"For the period Aug 1–Aug 31, 2026, the Service Availability baseline will be 99.90%. Monthly service credits payable to Customer for that period shall be limited to the lesser of 5% of Customer's monthly invoice for the Service or $75,000. Scheduled maintenance that has been notified to Customer at least 72 hours in advance and occurs within the agreed migration windows (Aug 10 00:00 UTC — Aug 12 23:59 UTC) shall be excluded from availability calculations. Unplanned incidents outside the migration window will be evaluated under the standard SLA."

Operational asks: Product needs to confirm whether we can set a maintenance marker that prevents automated monitoring from triggering credits for the specified windows (this is a common pattern). Also propose DocuSign flow for the one-page amendment.

If Greenline accepts the cap-of-5% OR $75k, I can get the amendment signed quickly.

—Laura
VP, Legal & Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term SLA exception + credit approach for Aug migration

Laura / Markus —

Finance ok with the 'lesser of 5% or $75,000' formulation as it bounds our exposure while respecting Greenline's ask. Two implementation notes from billing: 
1) If we use a dollar cap we should include an audit clause allowing Greenline to request a calculation of impacted tokens/requests; this keeps the reconciliation transparent.
2) Consider escrow: instead of paying credits immediately, we can place the credit amount into a short-term escrow (applied to Sep invoice) if both parties agree; this avoids cashflow surprises.

Operationally: Product needs to confirm that scheduled maintenance will be excluded from the automated availability checker (or we must manually reconcile). Markus — can you get product to confirm by EOD Tue so we can share a final amendment to Greenline?

Refs: HubSpot deal (see link)

—Ben
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Rosen <timothy.rosen@greenline.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term SLA exception + credit approach for Aug migration

Timothy —

Thanks for your patience while we reviewed internally. Summary of the proposed, time-limited amendment Redwood can offer for Aug 2026: 

1) Baseline: For the period Aug 1–Aug 31, 2026, Service Availability baseline will be 99.90% (temporary override of the standard 99.95%).
2) Credit cap: Monthly service credits for Aug 2026 will be limited to the lesser of 5% of Greenline's Redwood invoice for the Service or $75,000.
3) Maintenance carveout: Scheduled migration windows notified at least 72 hours in advance and occurring within Aug 10 00:00 UTC — Aug 12 23:59 UTC (including a 4-hour pre-warm buffer and 8-hour post-warm buffer for cache rehydration) will be excluded from availability calculations.
4) Reconciliation & escrow: Redwood is open to placing the capped credit amount into an escrow account to be applied to the next invoice pending reconciliation of impacts, as Ben suggested.

I've attached the one-page amendment (SLA amendment v2) and our credit workbook so you can see the mechanics. If this matches Greenline's needs, please confirm and we'll send a DocuSign for signature. If you prefer Option B (modified sliding with a higher threshold and 7.5% cap), say so and we'll outline that alternative.

Would you like a short alignment call next week or will you confirm by email?

—Markus
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla_amendment_greenline_v2.pdf, service_credit_calculator.xlsx
